slots.title: Jobless claims 206K beat 210K estimate
slots.body:
Initial jobless claims: **206K** actual vs **210K** estimate (prior **212K**).

That is the headline “initial filings” number—the count of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time in a week.

The **4-week average** printed **204K** vs a **200K** estimate (prior **199.8K**).

Continuing claims (people already on benefits) were **1,799K** vs **1,790K** estimated (prior **1,781K**).

All three prints were on the Aug. 20 calendar alongside retail earnings.

Which labor line do you watch first—initial claims or the 4-week average?

slots.title: Aug. 20 session recap
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished at 7,642.21, down 0.9% (65.77 points), with an intraday range between 7,639.01 and 7,699.96.

The Nasdaq Composite lost 1.0%, closing at 26,067.17, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.3% to 52,759.21, a 703.84-point drop.

The Russell 2000 declined 1.3% to 2,992.43, in line with the large-cap weakness rather than a small-cap bounce.

The VIX rose 7.5% to 16.01, up from a prior close of 14.89, as equity indexes slid.

At 12:30 p.m.
ET the U.S. released jobless claims: initial claims 206K vs 210K estimate (previous 212K), continuing claims 1,799K vs 1,790K estimate, and the four-week average at 204K vs 200K estimate.

Sector performance on Nasdaq tilted defensive in places: Real Estate led with an average gain of about 0.7%, while Industrials lagged at about -1.5%, Energy about -1.5%, Healthcare about -1.0%, and Technology was slightly positive at about +0.2%.

Walmart reported EPS $0.81 on revenue near $187.9B, both above estimates, yet $WMT still closed down 9.2% at $103.84 on volume of 83.5M shares.

Deere posted EPS $5.10 and revenue about $12.6B, above estimates, and $DE rallied 6.9% to $620.94.

Ross Stores beat on EPS ($2.66 vs $1.95 estimate) and revenue (~$6.26B vs ~$6.16B estimate), while $ROST still finished down 2.4% at $228.99.

Consumer-linked megacaps weakened with the tape:
- $AMZN -2.2%
- $HD -2.8%
- $COST -2.5%

to $933.51; $MRNA fell 23.5% to $133.32 among the session’s largest liquid declines.

Technology names were mixed against a down Nasdaq:
- $AMD +0.7%
- $NVDA -0.3%
- $MSFT -0.7%
- $GOOG -1.0%

to $338.20.

Cross-asset moves in the snapshot included Bitcoin up 1.2% to $73,897.79, the USO oil fund proxy up 2.8% to $134.54, gold futures roughly flat at $4,566.90 (-0.1%), Brent crude at $93.50 (-0.3%), and the dollar fund proxy UUP up 0.1% to $27.91.

Overseas indexes diverged: Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 1.0% to 65,574.88, the FTSE 100 edged up less than 0.1% to 10,748.16, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.9% to 25,698.49.

The latest Treasury yield snapshot in the feed is dated 2026-08-18, with the 10-year at 4.7% and the 2s10s spread at 0.52 percentage points; session headlines still described Treasury selling weighing on stocks Thursday.
